---
title: "Install"
---

## Requirements

EvoDAG needs Python 3.10 or newer and [NumPy](https://numpy.org). Those are
the only runtime dependencies. Part of the library is written in Cython, so
a compiled extension is shipped with it; the packaging files of the
repository declare Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 as the versions that are
built and tested, on Linux, macOS and Windows.

## From PyPI

```bash
pip install EvoDAG
```

When a prebuilt wheel exists for your platform and Python version, `pip`
installs it and nothing is compiled. Otherwise `pip` downloads the source
distribution and builds it, and then you need what is listed below under
[Building from source](#building-from-source).

## From conda-forge

```bash
conda config --add channels conda-forge
conda config --set channel_priority strict
conda install evodag
```

or, with `mamba`:

```bash
mamba install evodag
```

## Building from source

Building the extensions requires a C compiler, Cython 3 or newer and NumPy 2
or newer. Those build requirements are declared in `pyproject.toml`, so a
plain `pip install` of a checkout fetches Cython and NumPy by itself; the
compiler is the only thing you must provide (`gcc` or `clang` on Linux and
macOS, the Microsoft C++ build tools on Windows).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mgraffg/EvoDAG.git
cd EvoDAG
pip install .
```

For development, install in editable mode and rebuild the extensions after
changing a `.pyx` file:

```bash
pip install -e ".[test]"
python setup.py build_ext --inplace
python -m pytest -q tests
```

## Check the installation

```bash
python -c "import EvoDAG; print(EvoDAG.__version__)"
EvoDAG-train --version
```

The second command also confirms that the four console scripts
(`EvoDAG-params`, `EvoDAG-train`, `EvoDAG-predict` and `EvoDAG-utils`) are on
your `PATH`; they are described in the [Command line](cli.qmd) page.

## Optional packages

`tqdm` is used, when it is installed, to show a progress bar while an
ensemble is trained or evaluated. Nothing else is optional.
Graphviz is only needed if you want to turn the graph that
`Model.graphviz` writes into a picture (see [Python](python.qmd)).
